story.what_it_does: Can Fin Homes is a housing finance company that lends mainly for home purchase and construction. Its loan book was about ₹43,539 crore at September 2026, up roughly 10% on a year earlier. It earns the gap between what it charges borrowers and what it pays on its borrowings.
story.plans: Management targets about ₹13,000 crore of disbursements and 13-14% loan book growth for FY27, with credit cost near 10 bps. It also aims to raise direct sourcing and the share of self-employed customers (SENP), and to grow its branches and sales team. A new IT system (Project Tejas) was completed across all branches by October 1, 2026.
story.moat: The notes show a sponsor-bank link with Canara Bank, which provides term loans and deposits, plus strong liquidity and low bad loans (gross NPA 0.90%, net NPA 0.42%). Return on assets of about 2.4% is solid. The notes do not describe a clear structural advantage beyond this, and pricing competition and prepayments are pressing on growth.

scenarios.story: The IT system is now live everywhere, and disbursements recover toward the ₹3,500 crore Q3 target and beyond. Loan growth then moves toward the 13-14% goal while asset quality and credit cost stay low.

scenarios.story: Prepayments stay high, borrowing costs rise faster than lending rates, and weak monsoon or slower affordable housing demand hurts growth. The rising delinquency pool could also turn into real credit losses.
